From my side, I am concerned what consequences this might have for the ePD/DMA banner - would be glad if you could clarify this. *Please note that currently the decision was made to deploy it in Rides vertical only to measure impact, and the work to prepare the deployment is currently ongoing (in Rides only).* Only testing was done for Bolt Food, per my latest updates.

The first iteration of the banner only listed categories of third party trackers (i.e. Mixapnel, Appsflyer), and not specific cookies. The difference in safety & non-safety compensation guidelines is that for *safety cases we don’t give goodwill compensations* (e.g. 2eur compensation for a rider’s bad experience). This is because we don’t evaluate safety-related experiences in monetary value and sometimes the small sum compensation could even trigger the rider. However, in non-safety cases, since these situations are not as sensitive, we provide goodwill compensations to boost the user’s experience. 

This specific case about a driver using a phone is one of the few examples that don’t seem that sensitive, however, the compensation guidelines are applied for all events by the risk type, not by event categories.

Hi [~accountid:627cd41af29dcb0068f9650a] regarding your questions please see below :

* *Is it possible to have some branding materials on táxis in Portugal?* 

Yes, it is possible to have advertising outside and inside taxis.  

* *What are the legal obstacles here?* 
** *Advertising outside taxis:* Article 5 of [+Portaria 451/2023+|https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2023/12/24600/0006500069.pdf]
*** Advertising messages on the outside of taxis may only be displayed on the rear mudguards, on the side doors of the vehicle, excluding the windows, or on the roof. 
*** The upper part of the windscreen and the upper and lower parts of the rear window may bear the name of the company that owns the taxi or, if the taxi is equipped with a radio telephone or connected to a platform, the name of the entity operating the radio exchange or platform, the respective telephone number and the taxi's membership number to the exchange or platform, and these labels may also contain advertising notices. 
*** The signs referred to in the previous paragraph must be made of self-adhesive material, no more than 80 mm high, and must be placed in such a way as not to obstruct the driver's field of vision. 
*** A panel may be placed on the roof to display self-adhesive labels with advertising messages, in accordance with the indications and model in annex iv to this ordinance. 
*** If the panel referred to in the previous paragraph is placed, the luminous device must operate under the conditions set out in article 2 and may be placed in a centred position, on the upper front part of the panel, or in a lateral position, so that the luminous device is visible from the front and rear of the vehicle.
** *Advertising inside taxis:* no specific regulations
*** IMT in a similar situation (publicity in buses) has set the following guiding principles, which we recommend to be considered and adapted to the context of taxis: _“Inside: in the advertising spaces available for the purpose, as long as the visibility of the public road is not impaired, nor the visibility of the light signal to be used to determine the stop and restart of the vehicle, as well as the badge intended to identify the seats reserved for passengers with reduced mobility, emergency exits or other safety elements.”_
*** In addition, the general principles applicable to advertising must be observed, especially with regard to its content, as laid down in the Advertising Code (Decree-Law no. 330/90).

Hey [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] and [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] , thank you! This is very interesting!

I had a meeting with ops and the conclusion is the commission is not dynamic but binary 😂. 

The commission in PT is 25% and we communicated it to the fleets by email when we changed it 1 or 2 years ago. It is not part of t&c. We still need to fix the communication for new fleets, but we should have a look at that in the compliance project for TVDE we are deploying with OPS.

The idea of this new feature is that on some trips the algorythm will say that because this is a cheap trip no one will want to accept it, so let’s incentivise the trip acceptance by charging 15% (instead of the standard commission of 25%):

* This won’t change the final price to the consumer (no need for comms there)
* This will change the price the driver sees in the acceptance screen since we show net amount

Ops would prefer not to be transparent on the 15% because it will open the door to complaints: why are you charging 25% when you can and do charge at times 15%? I still think we should provide such transparency since we only act as a commercial agent. 

An alternative  that we think would be the easiest would be complying with the TVDE requirement regarding invoicing details. We would make it clear in the invoice the commission rate applied: we would provide the information to the passenger as mandated by the regulation in PT, inform the fleet (but not make easily visible) and add some language on reductions with the communication of the standard commission (currently at 25%). This is still WIP being discussed.  [^template_invoice.pdf]

Hi,

Just a reminder that according to the laws in Romania - GEO 49/2019 and Decision 572/2020 on ride-hailing, authorities have the right to request data *to make sure the ride-hailing laws are respected by the transport operators*. However, the laws do not explicitly mention the *Transport Police*. 

If we can keep in mind that in the conversations we previously had with the transport police, we committed to having a good collaboration with them. The police complained several times to the Govt that we "were not collaborating" enough.

*GEO 49/2019*:

Art. 26. -

*At the request of the authorities with powers in the field, provided by this emergency ordinance, the operator of the digital platform or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, will make available to them all the required information that it holds in relation to the performance of the activity by the operators of alternative transport through the digital platform. *Results*:

*Hypothesis 1:*  We expect that the *batched order rate increases* by 2 pp because order goes through both instant batching and batch routing systems, which increases the probability to get assigned to a batch.

The hypothesis is {color:#36B37E}*[ CONFIRMED ]*{color}. Increase in batch rate was mainly driven by same-provider batches (+11.5%).



*Hypothesis 2a:* We expect that *courier time per order will decrease* by 1.1% because average batched order courier time per order is 2.5min shorter compared to non-batched orders. 

*Hypothesis 2b:* We expect that *courier earnings per order will decrease* by 0.4% because average batched order courier earnings are 0.13€ lower compared to non-batched orders.

Hypotheses are partly {color:#36B37E}*[ CONFIRMED ]*{color}. There was +no statistically significant decrease in courier time per order+. However, we could observe a *decrease in CPO* even without reducing time spent on orders.

Additionally, we were able to observe a stat. significant *decrease in courier wait time at the provider* (-3 sec). We know that it improves courier experience, even though we have not yet quantified the business impact from lower wait times.



*Hypothesis 3a:* We expect that *pickup delay rate will increase* by 2.9% because average batched orders are picked up late 32% more often than non-batched orders. 

*Hypothesis 3b:* We expect that *drop-off delay rate will increase* by 4.3% because average batched orders are dropped-off late 48% more often than non-batched orders. 

Hypotheses are {color:#36B37E}*[ CONFIRMED ]*{color}. With increased batch rate the pickup and drop off delays increased. However, there were *no significant increase in CS tickets, refunds and failed orders.*



{color:#006644}*Roll-out decision*{color}

*Based on the analysis, we propose to roll out 2-step batching everywhere.* However, due to performance constraints the system needs to be modified for bigger cities. We suggest that:

* Roll out 2-step batching with multi-provider batches enabled in cities smaller than Vilnius (included).
* In Kyiv, Accra, Tallinn and Bucharest roll out 2-step batching in a way that during the Batch Routing step only same-provider batches are created, multi-provider batches can be created during Instant Batching step.

* *Article 249 of Criminal Procedure Code is an acceptable legal basis* - it applies to all the police inquiries to collect and secure evidence of crimes reported or known. IMO it should be included in the privacy knowledge database for PT

*PT*

*_Artigo 249.º_*
*_Providências cautelares quanto aos meios de prova_*
_1 - Compete aos órgãos de polícia criminal, mesmo antes de receberem ordem da autoridade judiciária competente para procederem a investigações, praticar os actos cautelares necessários e urgentes para assegurar os meios de prova._
_2 - Compete-lhes, nomeadamente, nos termos do número anterior:_
_a) Proceder a exames dos vestígios do crime, em especial às diligências previstas no n.º 2 do artigo 171.º, e no artigo 173.º, assegurando a integridade dos animais e a manutenção do estado das coisas, dos objetos e dos lugares;_
_b) Colher informações das pessoas que facilitem a descoberta dos agentes do crime e a sua reconstituição;_
_c) Proceder a apreensões no decurso de revistas ou buscas ou em caso de urgência ou perigo na demora, bem como adotar as medidas cautelares necessárias à conservação da integridade dos animais e à conservação ou manutenção das coisas e dos objetos apreendidos._
_3 - Mesmo após a intervenção da autoridade judiciária, cabe aos órgãos de polícia criminal assegurar novos meios de prova de que tiverem conhecimento, sem prejuízo de deverem dar deles notícia imediata àquela autoridade._

*_ENG_*

*_Article 249_*
*_Precautionary measures regarding evidence_*
_1 - Even before receiving an order from the competent judicial authority to carry out investigations, criminal police bodies shall be responsible for carrying out the necessary and urgent precautionary measures to secure evidence._
_2 - Under the terms of the previous paragraph, they are specifically responsible for_
_a) Carry out examinations of the traces of the crime, in particular the steps provided for in Article 171(2) and Article 173, ensuring the integrity of animals and the maintenance of the state of things, objects and places;_
_b)_ *_Gathering information from people to facilitate the discovery of the perpetrators of the crime and their reconstruction_*_;_
_c) Carry out seizures in the course of searches or searches or in the event of urgency or danger of delay, as well as adopt the precautionary measures necessary to preserve the integrity of the animals and to preserve or maintain the things and objects seized._
_3 - Even after the intervention of the judicial authority, it is up to the criminal police bodies to secure any new evidence they become aware of, without prejudice to the fact that they must immediately notify that authority._

* *Article 270, no. 1 and 4 of the Criminal Procedure Code and in Circular 6/2002 of the PGR of 11/03* [^Circulares _ Portal do Ministério Público - Portugal.pdf] *is an acceptable legal basis IMO* - it establishes that the crimes listed and in those conditions described in Circular 6/2002 the PSP is the entity in charge of investigation.

*_PT_*

*_Artigo 270.º_*
*_Actos que podem ser delegados pelo Ministério Público nos órgãos de polícia criminal_*
_1 - O Ministério Público pode conferir a órgãos de polícia criminal o encargo de procederem a quaisquer diligências e investigações relativas ao inquérito._

_…_
_4 - Sem prejuízo do disposto no n.º 2, no n.º 3 do artigo 58.º, no n.º 3 do artigo 243.º e no n.º 1 do artigo 248.º, a delegação a que se refere o n.º 1 pode ser efectuada por despacho de natureza genérica que indique os tipos de crime ou os limites das penas aplicáveis aos crimes em investigação._

*_ENG_*

*_Article 270_*
*_Acts that may be delegated by the Public Prosecutor's Office to criminal police bodies_*
_1 - The Public Prosecutor's Office may entrust criminal police bodies with the task of carrying out any steps and investigations related to the enquiry._
_4 - Without prejudice to the provisions of paragraphs 2 and 3 of article 58, paragraph 3 of article 243 and paragraph 1 of article 248, the delegation referred to in paragraph 1 may be carried out by means of a general order indicating the types of offence or the limits of the penalties applicable to the offences under investigation._

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *17 January 2025.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. No âmbito da monitorização contínua dos padrões de qualidade do serviço, foi identificado um comportamento irregular por parte de um motorista, que consistia em aceitar viagens e, em seguida, permanecer parado no mesmo local ou dirigir-se noutra direção, aguardando que o cliente efetuasse o cancelamento da viagem em vez de o próprio o fazer. Este tipo de prática compromete a experiência do cliente e viola os padrões de qualidade estipulados.

Foram enviadas várias comunicações, tanto ao motorista como à frota responsável, alertando para este comportamento inadequado e as suas consequências. Contudo, estas comunicações foram ignoradas, não tendo havido qualquer alteração no padrão de conduta identificado. A evidência de tais comunicações, bem como dos comportamentos detetados, pode ser confirmada através dos print screens anexados.

Como parte do processo habitual, foi dado um período para que o motorista corrigisse as práticas identificadas. Este procedimento inclui avisos prévios antes de qualquer ação definitiva, como bloqueios ou suspensões. No entanto, os avisos não resultaram, tendo o comportamento persistido. Assim, e em conformidade com os procedimentos internos, foi necessário proceder à suspensão do acesso do motorista.

A situação é ilustrada na viagem anexada nos prints, que demonstra claramente o padrão de comportamento descrito. Este caso reforça o compromisso com a manutenção da qualidade do serviço, assegurando que todas as medidas são tomadas para corrigir condutas que prejudiquem o cliente e a reputação da plataforma.

:green-check: Adopting the query of {{Driver Step 2}}:

*Handling the duplicates*

For some technical reason, Driver step 2 sometimes can be sent twice from the same device. Therefore, we see duplicate events in both ga4_analytics and fleet_driver_registration_event

Options to handle the duplicates are:

* Rewrite the whole data for the period we might actively be using for experiments and MMM (1.5-2Y) => might be quite expensive
* Ensure that just deleting the duplicates within one day makes them minor (and still use merge+window incremental logic)=> see description below

In this [notebook|https://bolt-datascience.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/4326894895484681?o=3829506390716583#command/7862560943565373] (and results in this [spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18LuZ41ifFaHy_j0vsUxswcM4tQQ-ivW4gzeBpr0lrOg/edit?usp=sharing]) we show that:

* 70%+ of all duplicates happen within one day
** meaning that independent of the refresh window, we will be able to cover majority of duplicates
* 98.5%+ users do not repeat their Driver Step 2 on the day other than the same day
** meaning that our error in overall metric will not exceed 1.5%
* Android and iOS the number of duplicates almost proportional to their overall distribution
** Because to us is important not just to have the totals correct, but be sure that Android/iOS relation does not skew, we can be sure that minor duplicates are affecting both platforms

Additionally, we are using max (i.e. latest event):

* With merge+window incremental refresh it will guarantee less duplicates, always selecting the latest of the duplicates.
* Example: User sent two events: on 01.04 and 03.04. 
** If we are using min:
*** While the user is inside the update window, we will attribute him to 01.04
*** But when update window is >= 01.04, the user’s event stays in the table
*** 03.04 appears as not-duplicated
** If we are using max:
*** The user is always assigned to 03.04. and not duplicated



*The query*

{noformat}WITH bq as (
SELECT user_id as bq_user_id, max_by(device.operating_system, event_date) as os
FROM bigquery_spark.ga4_analytics 
WHERE event_name = 'Driver Completed Step 2'
AND event_date >= '2024-09-01' -- date_sub(date'{{ var("data_interval_start") }}', {{- mart_ads_days_back_overwrite() -}})
AND event_date <= '2024-12-31' -- date'{{ var("data_interval_end") }}'
GROUP BY 1
),

fdre_deduplicated as (

SELECT driver_registration_log_id, max(created_date) as created_date
FROM ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_registration_event
WHERE step = 'step_2'
AND created_date >= '2024-09-01' -- date_sub(date'{{ var("data_interval_start") }}', {{- mart_ads_days_back_overwrite() -}})
AND created_date <= '2024-12-31' -- date'{{ var("data_interval_end") }}'
GROUP BY 1
),

backend as (
SELECT e2.created_date be_created_date,  city.city_name, city.country_name, concat('lead-driver-', hash) as be_user_id, city as be_city, e2.created_date
FROM ng_public_spark.fleet_driver_registration_log fdrl
LEFT OUTER JOIN fdre_deduplicated e2 ON e2.driver_registration_log_id=fdrl.id
LEFT OUTER JOIN core_models_spark.dim_city city ON fdrl.city_id = city.city_id -- {{ source('dbt_common', 'dim_city') }} AS city
WHERE e2.created_date >= fdrl.created_date
AND source = 'driver_portal'
)

SELECT 'Driver Step 2' as metric_name, 
  be_created_date as date_date, 
  city_name, 
  country_name, 
  lower(os) as os, 
  count(distinct be_user_id) as metric_value, 
  current_timestamp() AS last_ingested_ts
FROM backend 
LEFT JOIN bq ON bq.bq_user_id = backend.be_user_id
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5{noformat}

By default, all Lattice-based apps display notifications (including error notifications) in the bottom left corner. We (builder owners) would like to keep this behaviour in the builder for consistency. As for the time the error is displayed, we'll increase the display time to *15 seconds*. This time should be enough to read the error message in most of the cases. Keeping error messages forever would increase the task complexity and implementation time as this change affects {{admin-framework-components}} functionality (which needs to be either extended or we have to implement notifications on our own). That would affect the scoring of the task, and we might not get the change anytime soon. By increasing the time to display, we can add some value right away with relatively low effort.

Hi [~accountid:712020:46da73ea-bcbb-4b69-8e3e-ac27402d61bc] ! 

And thank you [~accountid:5f2d0e2efa591d0015f85227] for your insights! 

From privacy side the preferred option would be to share the insurer’s details with the injured party since this option would not entail any personal data sharing of the rider. However I understand that this process would not always be preferred by the FO themselves as they may not want to activate insurance. 

So if that option is not feasible and this data sharing really would improve the process in PT, then it is possible to share the riders information (name, e-mail, phone number) with the FO +based on the consent of the rider.+ This means that when a case “my Bolt was in an accident” is raised then we ask for the consent as follows: 

* Would you agree that Bolt shares your name, email and phone number with the respective Fleet Owner? They will use your contact details to contact you regarding the accident. Your consent will be valid until the issue is resolved or until you choose to withdraw your consent by making a request to our Support Team. 
Please send ‘Agree to share’ if you agree and ‘Do not share’ if you disagree.

** If they respond Agree to share/YES → we can share
** If they respond Do not share/NO → we do not share
** If they do not respond anything or are unclear → we do not share. 

I want to point out that if CS is handling these cases and collecting consent manually, then there is a risk of human error. Meaning that if the agent does not get the required consent, then any data sharing that would take place is without a legal basis and therefore be deemed as a data breach. In addition it is also always necessary to check whether the details will be provided to the correct Fleet Owner (as we have had similar incidents stemming from human errors where details are shared with a wrong counterparty). 

So if this ends up as a KB Article which covers the process then it has to very clear that consent is always required and without that any data sharing cannot place.

+*STATUS*+

* *Deadline*: 12 February 2025
* *Request*: Driver wants to know: (1) the contents of a complaint lodged by a passenger; (2) legal grounds for withholding this information; (3) the outcome / decision relating to this complaint; (4) correction / deletion of the complaint if it is unconfirmed; and (5) for ADM information relating to the complaint.
* *Background*:
** On 12 January, a Ukrainian rider reported ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/504312870]) a UA driver about driver being intoxicated and speeding. 
*** “_The driver was driving very fast, although I made a comment that I didn't like it. He was talking to someone on the phone. Very sudden unclear movements, loud heavy music in the car, it seemed that the driver was under the influence of substances_”
*** “_The passenger reported that the driver immediately started driving very fast, when she asked him to slow down, he loudly said “why?”. after that, he slowed down a bit and started talking on the phone, but it was on a stand. she believes that he could have been under the influence of drugs, because there were very sudden movements, loud music and hyper-concentration_.”
** On the same day, Bolt reached out to the driver ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/504343447]) to get their side of the story (flagged to the driver that Bolt has received a “_complaint from a passenger that you were probably under the influence of alcohol_”).
*** Driver claimed rider must be referring to the small of antiseptic. They denied the allegations.
*** As a result of this, the block on the driver’s account was lifted. Driver informed of this, and that ”_We also received a report from a passenger that you were also speeding during the trip_”.
*** Outcome pf investigation (inetrnal) was: “_[12/01/2025] CS Safety closed, Cannot Be Confirmed, Driver At Fault, 2nd Report, Warning_”.
** On the same day, the driver asked “_tell us, at least, what is the essence of the complaint?… since the complaint is against me, I have the right to know its content_.”
*** CS responded “_We have already informed you of the content of the complaint, namely that you were intoxicated and speeding_”. CS also flagged that we have just raised it to the driver to get their side of the story, and we are not accusing them.
*** Driver not happy with this and asked “_I am asking you to provide me with the content of the passenger's appeal to analyse the events of that trip_”.
*** CS cited GDPR as a reason for not providing more specific info (although phrased this as sharing data with third parties, which is not _fully_ correct). Driver asked to be provided with where in the GDPR this is set out. What follows is effectively a tit-for-tat, in which CS (unfortunately) keeps asserting that the driver is a ‘third party’ here (and therefore that it is not their personal data, which is incorrect), which was not approved by Privacy.. This has led to unnecessary escalation.
** Driver then asked “_Is this personal data processed using algorithms?_”
** On 13 Jan, driver specified that their GDPR requests were as follows (as their relate to the complaint from the rider):
*** “_the essence and what exactly in my actions made the passenger file a complaint_”
*** “_my explanation_”
*** “_what decision was made on the incident (because there will be 2 options for the development of events)_”
*** “_If, after processing the PD, it is decided that the passenger's complaint is not confirmed, then I, as a subject, have the right to demand the termination of processing of these PD, CORRECTION, destruction of these PD, etc. especially if their further processing with automatic decision-making may adversely affect me as a person, my life_.”
** Later that day, the driver sent out a lengthy explanation on their views regarding the position under the GDPR.
*** Complaint about a driver is a driver’s personal data, and no ‘third parties’ are involved here (this is correct).
*** Driver acknowledges that a balancing exercise is required (“_The driver has the right to know that his or her data is being processed, but the company may not disclose the context of the complaint if it violates the passenger's rights_”).
*** Company should act in accordance with Article 21 re objection to processing (particularly where processing is unfair or unreasonable).
*** Driver believes that the passenger complaint is being used in the context of ADM. Driver has right to be informed about ADM, to request additional info on the logic of ADM, and to have the chance to appeal it / ensure it is subject to human review.
** We have also previous received DSARs from this driver from last year, for their order history ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-27293|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-27293|smart-link] and [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-40305|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-40305|smart-link] ), and for all of their data ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/servicedesk/projects/LSS/queues/custom/766/LSS-40138|https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/servicedesk/projects/LSS/queues/custom/766/LSS-40138|smart-link] ). * *Tracker*: Registered on Cognito ([Link|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/datasubjectrightsrequeststracker/entries/1-all-entries/961])
* *Analysis*:
** *Contents of complaint*: We should not provide anything beyond what we have already provided, as it could be used to identify the passenger (in any case, there is not much more to provide). 
** *Explanation for withholding*: We should explain that this is the driver’s personal data, but we need to protect the rights and freedoms of third parties (which here is the passenger). We should apologise for the previous confusion of terminology.
** *Outcome*: We should reiterate that the account was unblocked and the driver was issued with a warning, per Bolt processes.
** *Correction / deletion*: We can leverage language from [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-41955|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-41955] which makes a similar point, and say: “_Bolt allows passengers to issue complaints, based on the passengers' own experiences, against drivers to provide additional reassurance to passengers and to provide a safe and accountable marketplace environment. It is therefore of the upmost importance that records of complaints are maintained on our platform in accordance with applicable laws_”. This should cover both the ‘inaccuracy’ point and the objection issue.
** *ADM info*: It seems that someone from CS Safety reviewed this case, and so (subject to confirmation) I think we have strong grounds for arguing that A22 does not apply here.
* *Next* *Steps*:

** Draft response.
** Ensure the response is sent from ‘Bolt Privacy Team’, rather than Bolt.

Conclusions, [~accountid:6358f0a9548f1fe6f0c61397]: 

* According to Sunday, the proposed system of having separate WD entities for each part revision of a part is already in place for mechanical parts, but the revision naming scheme is complex.
* What could be done better:
** Retaining the revision history of parts in BOM (What we already have in the IOT BOM catalogue)
** Part names must be clearer for suppliers. The description field is not added to POs and the part numbers are confusing to suppliers.
** Issues from operations part:
*** Tracking consumption is problematic
** Parts display part compatibility to a vehicle, but not vice-versa.
** Ordering development parts is confusing from the Excel table of mechanical parts. Sharing incoming revision or new part development info with procurement would lessen the problem. Sunday and Omar liked the idea of having a PCR (Product Change Request) process in place. Even a simple one would suffice. I can support with this.
* My main takeaways:
** We should continue with developing separate WD part entities for different IOT parts. We would move away from having a common name for an IOT part type, and rather have separate part names for all IOT revisions, versions, etc. Who do I talk to from here on?
** A PCR process can have value for engineering overall. I can make a prototype and present it.
** No timeline in place for these activities as of yet, since we need to align task priorities at this time.

Hello Justus! 

My apologies for the delay in the response. 🙏 Regarding your questions - the local OPS team sent out the first informational e-mail in June 2023 when the suspension for the low acceptance rate was implemented in the LT market. Later on, communication was regularly sent out to couriers, the frequency of such communication I cannot state, but it was pretty regularly based on the frequent case flow in regards to this topic. The increase of such cases would occur on Monday-Tuesday as noted by the agent. In late October/the beginning of November 2024, OPS member informed that part of their tasks were undertaken by the global CS team as part of the HQ project. The fate of the communication to the couriers remains unknown. However, based on the couple of cases that I managed to find, it appears the educational messages were sent out ([example 1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/461984501], [example 2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/461925829]). 

The last screenshot is from the Telegram courier’s group, it is taken from a post in the autumn (around September-October). I checked the last couple of weeks, and no such communication was provided anymore. 

In terms of the volumes, without further analysis, I cannot answer a clear number of tickets for this particular topic as we have no stats for this. But using last week’s DSAT information, which isn’t a full volume reflection, there are 7 DSATs in LT with _My account is blocked unfairly_ issue tag. Certainly, there are more incoming cases with such topics, they just don’t end in a DSAT. The quality team and the team leaders receive comments from agents every day and for some time now, agents have been saying that this process is complicated and unclear - this is the heart of the issue, couriers want to know how to improve, and agents do not know what tips can be shared. Hi team,

* *How can we be sure that drivers do not create new profiles and aren’t abusing permanent blocks, a new-driver bonus, or resetting their statistical metrics?*
** When registering a new driver, duplicates must be checked. If the driver had a block in their previous account, registration can be rejected. For the new-driver bonus - the referral code can be removed when registering a new driver if the driver already completed rides with a previous account. And for resetting their statistical metrics - unfortunately, this can’t be prevented, however, we haven’t seen examples that drivers would be doing that.
* *If driver later wish to work again, they must create a new profile, as we cannot "reuse" a deleted profile. Could you clarify the reasoning behind this policy and how we can explain it to drivers?*
** When we delete the driver’s account, we inform them that their data will be deleted. When the driver requests to create a new account, we cannot restore a previous one, as the data is no longer in the system, so they need to register again. So we can repeat the same message we already sent to the driver when deleting their account, and explain that their data is deleted.
*** *_Internal information_*_: We store some data under the law and we have a legal right to keep it if it's necessary (e.g. to defend a legal claim). However, this data cannot be used to restore the account._ 
* *For hard-blocked drivers who request account deletion and later attempt to re-register, what can we tell them about the retained data that allows us to identify their prior block status?*
** As mentioned above, we store some data under the law and we have a legal right to keep it if it's necessary. However, this information shouldn’t be shared with drivers, and if you ever have a situation where you need to explain this to a driver, you should ask for the Privacy team’s advice on how to formulate a correct response.
* *For drivers who voluntarily delete their accounts but return later, how do we explain that they are not eligible for new driver campaigns due to their previous registration?*
** Tell them directly as it is - the driver can’t get a new driver bonus because they are not new, they already worked with us.

I hope that answers your questions and feel free to contact me if there’s anything else.

h2. Dashboard Camera Use in Norway

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
h4. *Legal Framework*

# *Primary Regulations*:
#* General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), as implemented by the Norwegian Personal Data Act (Personopplysningsloven).
#* Guidelines and practices from the Norwegian Data Protection Authority (NDPA) and the Norwegian Privacy Appeals Board.
# *Workplace-specific Regulations* (not directly applicable but offer insights):
#* Norwegian Labour Act (Arbeidsmiljøloven).
#* Norwegian Regulation on Camera Surveillance in Businesses (Forskrift om Kameraovervåking i virksomhet).
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
h4. *Key recommendations*

# Conduct a *legitimate interest assessment* to evaluate the necessity and proportionality of camera use.
# Ensure *minimal data collection* by limiting recording to short durations and targeted areas.
# Use *clear signage* on e-scooters and update the privacy policy with detailed information about camera usage.
# Implement a *strict retention policy* in line with the NDPA's guidelines.
# Avoid audio recording entirely.
# Develop *clear internal procedures* for handling recordings, including access control and deletion protocols.
{panel}

h4. 

h4. *Privacy Requirements for Dashcam Use*

# *Legitimacy of Surveillance*:
#* Legitimate interests (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) are the most relevant legal basis.
#* Proportionality and necessity must be demonstrated.
#* Time-limited activation of cameras (e.g., during theft or accidents) may serve as mitigating measures.
#* Limit the camera's field of view and recording duration to what is strictly necessary.
#* Avoid capturing unrelated areas or subjects.
# *Allowed Locations for Surveillance*:
#* Surveillance of public spaces by private companies is generally restricted, but:
#** Insignificant areas of public space may be captured.
#** Surveillance on public transportation +may be justified for safety reasons+ (analogous to e-scooter use).
# *Information and Transparency*:
#* Clearly inform individuals about surveillance via visible signs on the e-scooters.
#* Provide detailed information in a privacy notice accessible through the website and app.
# *Data Retention*:
#* Preventive recordings (e.g., theft mode): Retain for up to *7 days*, unless an incident requires further action.
#* Reactive recordings (e.g., accidents): Retain until the incident is resolved or reported, up to *30 days* unless a longer retention period is justified.
# *Data Use and Disclosure*:
#* Restrict access to recordings to authorised personnel.
#* Disclosure to third parties requires:
#** Consent from affected individuals.
#** A legal obligation (e.g., police investigations).
#* Audio recording is not permitted and may constitute a criminal offense.

Thank you for clarification [~accountid:6257f823ed2b3e0074fd8114] 

So here we have couple of different paths on the table how to resolve the payment journey. Fraud pushes for decisions pre-authorise (pre-book funds) based on information on pricing predictions - this means if we want to have the option to pre-book some funds at order placing, there needs to be a prompt on the pricing set up side. We can double check these flows and what currently is abled if you make the test ride requests. 

After the journey ends there are two option for us to cater towards: we could keep the (_suspected_) preauth (35€) and add the further charges (full price - preauth) to users debt balance. This option will ensure we will always keep the initial booked amount but will result in users having debt for the rest of the accumulated amount that is harder and more friction to recover - it will also heavily limit our possibility to track bad payments and/or recovery. 

The other option is to release the first booked amount and compiling a full new charge for the total of the journey. So as an example, if we first were able to book 35€ and final price for trip is 70€ then we release the 35€ and make a new attempt to charge 70€ altogether. This has a higher risk of failing due as we have checked the user only against the booked sum for available funds and their situation can change between the start and finish of the trip. A popular scheme is to also block their payment card meanwhile so we will not be able to charge anything else. 

 Just to note, we are not able to control or manipulate any of the pricing set up here → meaning we can’t on the fraud side fix how much and when we charge or book, this information always comes in from pricing set up/log. As a result we also don’t have the opportunity to revert to a fixed pricing: e.g if a trip ends up at 105€, we can’t say charge only 70€, we can only attempt to charge the 105€ fixed or alternatively make the decision to keep first booking (35€) and add the rest to user debt (70€).

The option of release booking and try capture full amount is better for this scenario in my opinion but I want to reiterate that both have their pros and cons as we are working with options designed for other matters and do not have any way to be secure for price jumps between the 1st and 2nd hour (anytime we go over first hour // pre-booked amount). 

We’d need to also set up a manual followup to these trips with payment problems that exceed 2h/70€ as our automatic detection and actions can only assist in case of full price problems and as I understand the drivers will still need to receive earnings for anything under the 2h. Hi [~accountid:63934c5700cb2fc3f98c7e42],

Buying the cars through Bolt Services LT to carry out a subsequent sale to LHV may trigger some risk for Bolt Services LT, because this entity would bear LT VAT. Such an input VAT qualifies as tax deductible for Bolt Services LT, but then the company would not charge local VAT in the subsequent transfer of goods to LHV, as such a transaction would qualify as an intra-community transfer of goods (0%).

Therefore, Bolt Services LT would end up having a considerable VAT credit, which may be challenged by the LT Tax authorities as non-deductible since such a credit is not linked with any sale subject to LT VAT.

Perhaps I’m being too conservative, but under such a scenario we’d have to delve deeper into the tax implications arising from such a scheme.

As a result, after deployment, the scooter remained in one place and did not send any coordinates. In the app, it appears with the coordinates where it was deployed, which differ from the actual deployment location.
We have checks in place:
1. If the IoT scooter’s coordinates have not been updated, deployment should not be allowed.
2. A scooter cannot be deployed inside the WH without a warning on the app screen.
I spoke with the Scale team and explained the case to them. However, after reviewing all the logs and my sequence of actions together, we couldn’t identify the issue. The only thing they mentioned is that they performed a refactoring in November, and it might not be possible to reproduce the issue now.
What I was able to reproduce on Prelive:
1. Getting an error if the scooter’s coordinates haven’t been updated for more than 3 minutes (but according to the logs, the scooter in Kyiv didn’t send https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-micromobility/vehicles/iot/view/776944?tab=logs&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A0%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22lines%22%3A10000%2C%22from_ts%22%3A1731974400%2C%22to_ts%22%3A1732147200%7D%7Dcoordinates> all day).
2. Deploying a scooter with the charger’s coordinates—if it doesn’t send coordinates afterward, it will be displayed in one place on the map and in another place in the app.

*Clarification*

*Context*

This task is mainly meant for Alter Automation developer owners, not the DBREs. We need to find pipelines that run excessively long and fast, so Kibana logs are still there to debug them.

The definition of “long” is if the pipeline runs more than 72h

{noformat}SELECT 
    approx_percentile(DATE_DIFF('minute', created, finished_at), 0.95) AS p95_working_time_minutes,
    AVG(DATE_DIFF('minute', created, finished_at)) AS avg_working_time_minutes
FROM 
    glue.ng_public.alter_orchestrator_pipeline
WHERE 
    status = 'completed' -- Adjust this condition based on how successful pipelines are defined.
    AND finished_at IS NOT NULL 
    AND created IS NOT NULL;{noformat}

p95 1215 (~20h)
p99 4351 (~72h)
avg 246.5 (~4h)

*Recommended solution*

* Create a corn that runs once in an hour  {{ SELECT * alter_orchestrator_pipeline WHERE DATE_DIFF('minute', created, finished_at) > 4320 AND status='in_progress'}} 
* Use {{untois}} to send Slack notifications about the pipeline that there is a pipeline that is running more than 72h.
* Use Redis to silence the alert for 24h, if tomorrow the pipeline is still running, send the alert again.

Like this this task should doable < 1mw

It is not possible to add 5 personal days to an employee who does not meet the criteria of the Time Off Plan in Workday. The current eligibility rules that workday follows are: 1) Employee is in Estonia, 2) employment type is _regular_. 

Instead, we could add the 5 days on top of annual leave and the employee and manager will have to agree on how they differentiate the time off requests between the two of them. Our internal policy and payment for annual leave are similar enough that there wouldn't be issues with losing pay. The only difference is that personal days do not carry over to the next year. Thus, they would need to agree on how they track this. 

Would the proposed solution work for you?

Best
Alice, People Ops

To ensure compliance with data protection laws, we will need to conclude a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) for this collaboration, as mentioned before. Below is an explanation of why the following data points are considered personal data under the law:

* *pickup point: address, longitude and latitude:* These can identify specific locations that are often associated with an individual’s home, workplace, or other identifiable places.
* *dropoff point: address, longitude and latitude:* Similar to the pickup point, this data reveals personal movement patterns and can be linked to identifiable individuals.
* *ride price*: When analyzed alongside other data, ride pricing may be linked to specific trips or individuals.
* *ride distance and time*: These provide detailed insights into travel behavior, especially when combined with pickup and dropoff data.
* *accepted ride timestamp*: This can reveal routines and habits, making it personally identifiable when paired with other data points.

Generally, the data is okay to be shared, but we’d like to put in place necessary safeguards to make sure that we share data properly. And signing a DSA would serve that purpose 🙂

I've started working on it. However, after a number of  💩  I've encountered on my way, I decided that a separate refactoring of this doesn't make sense, the tech debt there is just too much, it needs to be scrapped and written from scratch.

To name the reasons

* {{interaction_metadata}} must be kept backward-compatible (due to old event payloads) so I can only deprecate things, cannot remove them from there (unless I want to run some backfill cron)
* moving the relevant data to the {{additional_inputs}} property in the event data would have be done in 2 steps (first duplicate the data, then remove it from {{interaction_metadata}} and start relying on {{additional_inputs}} once old interaction expire)
* looks like {{additional_inputs}} is not only built based on {{interaction_metadata}} - for SSAT for example it's built based on some snapshot metadata ({{priceAndCurrencyMeta}})
* I thought I could include that metadata in {{additional_inputs}} but then it's used in 3 different places , not only for {{additional_inputs}}, but also as:
** translation params for the {{options}} keys
** to build {{additional_interaction_texts}}, which is another property specific to SSAT interaction
* I thought I could also add {{translation_props}} to the event data to satisfy the first and move the {{additional_interaction_texts}} to {{additional_inputs}} to keep things generic
** that would require modifying frontend logic, also in 2 steps (first to consume new props while falling back to old props, then to cleanup relying on the old props)
* ... but then it turns out that SSAT is a kind of one-to-many interaction which has multiple variants (not only all sorts of refunds but also {{DELETE_ACCOUNT}}, {{DELIVERY_CANCEL_ORDER}}) and a different kind of {{additional_inputs}} ,
** this "different kind" of additional_inputs essentially allow defining {{additional_inputs}} for each possible response
** these {{additional_inputs}} aren't defined for all possible responses, or even all possible refunds, but only those refunds which allow refund kind selection in the second step
** ... which that makes me unable to move it there

All in all, it started to feel more and more like putting a lipstick on a pig, something which would take a much more significant effort than anticipated while not resolving the fundamental issues.

It’s possible to run the DRP against prelive. Use the following command to run Hopp web-app:

{{yarn start:prelivehopp}}
